question_text: Look at the LDO block diagram in Image 1. If the reference voltage (V_ref) feeds into the NEGATIVE (-) terminal of the error amplifier, and the measured feedback voltage (V_fb) feeds into the POSITIVE (+) terminal, is the pass transistor a PMOS or an NMOS?
answer_text: It is a PMOS pass transistor.
explanation_text: Here is the logic: If V_out spikes too high, V_fb also goes high. Because V_fb is connected to the positive (+) non-inverting terminal, the error amplifier's output voltage increases. To bring V_out back down, we need the pass transistor to choke the current (increase its resistance). A PMOS transistor turns OFF (increases resistance) as its gate voltage increases toward its source voltage. Therefore, this error amp polarity specifically controls a PMOS!
bonus_question_text: What is the main disadvantage of a PMOS LDO compared to an NMOS LDO?
bonus_answer_text: PMOS transistors typically have higher ON-resistance (R_DS(on)) and worse conductivity than NMOS transistors for a given physical size. To handle high currents, a PMOS must be physically much larger, taking up more silicon area.
